To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the genome sequences of Pseudomonas strains were used for discovery of previously unknown CLPs, which are involved in the lifestyle of P. syngae and P. fluorecens strains.

we discovered a new gene cluster involved in CLP biosynthesis in the model plant beneficial bacterium P. fluorecens SBW2 and showed that the CLP produced by this gene cluster plays an important role in the lifestyle of this bacterium.
Genome mining has enabled the identification of previously unknown gene clusters in Pseudomonads involved in the biosynthesis of cyclic lipopeptides.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of novel CLP gene clusters from plant beneficial and pathogenic bacteria, and with the characterization of the role of CLP production in the lifestyle of Pseudomonads.
the discovery of novel CLP gene clusters and the identification of the biological functions of these CLPs in the model strains P. syringae and P. fluorescens.
the development and use of genomic tools for the identification of new gene clusters and the elucidation of their biological role in Pseudomonads.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the genome‐based discovery of new gene clusters and traits in P. syngae B728a and P. syringae DC3000 and the discovery of new traits in P. fluorescens SBW 25 and P. fluorescense Pf0‐1 is a significant contribution to the understanding of the biology of Pseudomonas.
genome‐based discovery, structural prediction and functional analysis are powerful tools for the identification of novel CLPs in Pseudomonads.

genome mining may be used to predict the presence of gene clusters and traits, but that the presence of a gene cluster is not sufficient for the production of a compound, nor for a biological activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the genome‐based discovery of CLP gene clusters, their structure prediction, functional analyses and chemical characterization of the metabolite in Pseudomonads is reported.
we have discovered a new CLP antibiotic from Pseudomonas SBW25, which is a plant beneficial strain.
we have identified a new CLP gene cluster in a plant‐associated Pseudomonas strain.
The main takeaway from our work is that
genome mining may be an efficient approach for discovery of unknown gene cluster and traits in plant‐associated microbes that may be highly relevant for the lifestyle of the microbes.

the genome‐based prediction of CLP biosynthetic gene clusters is a valuable strategy for the discovery of new CLPs in Pseudomonads and that CLP production is a widespread phenomenon among Pseudomonads.
the identification of novel gene clusters in the genomes of Pseudomonas strains can lead to the discovery of novel metabolites that can be important for the lifestyle of the producing strain.
